utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation still applies, Mr. Hutsch, as you have come used to the idea by now. It should be possible today, should you wish, for you to speak in German, but the questions will be put to you in English and it will be up to you. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Last night when we left off, I wanted to ask you a few more questions about what you say you observed in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th, in particular about your suggestions of having met in the village Mr. Tarculovski, Johan, and Mr. Stojanov, Goran. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that, again, nothing in your notes of the 12th mention you meeting either of those persons. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that you have mentioned to the Office of the Prosecutor that you, prior to that event, you had said to have met, or to have seen in any case, Mr. Tarculovski on a number of occasions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember how many times you had seen? Was it one time, two times?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: One time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall where that was?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's already in the -- in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that the meeting which you have mentioned which took place in Tetovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did we speak about the 12th, or did we speak about the general term.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am asking you -- you indicated that you said you saw Mr. Tarculovski in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated also that you had met Mr. Tarculovski on at least one prior occasion, prior to this event. This is the 27th of June, 2007, page 2772. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that you had mentioned meeting Mr. Tarculovski in the village or the town of Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you have suggested that the person who introduced you to Mr. Tarculovski was Mr. Goran Zdravkovski. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you remember what the position of Mr. Zdravkovski was at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was the commander of a special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the Tigers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you remember anyone else present on that occasion when you said you met Mr. Tarculovski through Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The manager of the -- not the manager. The manager of the textile factory Teteks, and the man, he was also manager of the hotel Tetovo Theke.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: An aside from this occasion, when you said you met Mr. Tarculovski in the town or city of Tetovo, do you recall any other occasions when you met Mr. Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another time when he was guarding the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall mentioning to the Office of the Prosecutor, in your statement, that you had several conversations and interviews with Goran Zdravkovski? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I met him sometimes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you recall specifically saying that you had several conversations and interviews with him?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had interviews with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you publish any of those interviews, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a interview like you tried to -- to make now. It was more background speech where he was explaining me the general situation in the Tetovo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't the situation that you have never met with Mr. Zdravkovski, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suggest that we can, first, take him face to face to me; and, second, is that we can ask the manager and the receptionist of the Tetovo Theke hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth that you never met Mr. Tarculovski in Tetovo in the month of March 2001, as you claimed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: March or June?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the statement, Your Honour, suggests the month of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was it March or June, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: March.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the case, Mr. Hutsch, that you never met Mr. Tarculovski in Tetovo in the month of March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Hutsch, that Mr. Tarculovski at the time was the body-guard of the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware what he was doing in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Hutsch, that you have invented this story. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, we have two other witnesses, and I think we can -- we can go further with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to show you a statement, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 1D309.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, what will appear in front of you is a statement of Mr. Goran Zdravkovski, who you've mentioned and who you said introduced you to Mr. Tarculovski, and it was a statement taken by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski earlier this year. I would like to read to you the statement. You can see that, at paragraph 1, he was asked to give a statement by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski. His name, date of birth is in paragraph 2; his father's name. Then, at paragraph 4, it says: "On 25th of May of 2001, I became commander of the Tigers unit." First, I'd like to draw your attention to the date, Mr. Hutsch. It is the 25th of May, 2001. Can you see that? Mr. Hutsch, can you see paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in fact, in March of 2001, he was not the commander of the Tigers unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we go down to paragraph 5, it says this: "I was asked to comment on the following paragraph from a statement which I was told was written in the statement, as printed, of a German journalist named Franz-Josef Hutsch. It is paragraph 163 of the statement. "At the time, Johan Tarculovski was the commanding policemen in Tetovo. We met on several occasions when I had conversations and interviews with Goran Zdravkovski, former command of the Tigri unit. "In the course of our conversation, I said I wanted to go to the front line in Tetovo, as near as possible. He accompanied me as far as the main road passing by the orthodox church in Tetovo. A unit of police reservists was positioned in the street. "Goran Zdravkovski introduced me to Johan Tarculovski. On that occasion, Tarculovski and I talked about the current situation. I visited the positions which were under the command of Tarculovski. He was wearing a camouflage police uniform. I did not hear anything about his rank. I saw police reservists and armed civilians at these positions." So this is taken from your own statement, Mr. Hutsch. Then, Mr. Zdravkovski was asked a few questions, and he said this: "Firstly, I want to say that I never met Franz-Josef Hutsch. I never gave a interview or talked to this person in Tetovo or anywhere else." So, do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that, at least as far as this statement is concerned, there is a pretty strong discrepancy between that you gave here and what Mr. Zdravkovski is saying. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suggest that we will call up Mr. Tastanovski, Milesav Tastanovski, and the manager from the Theke hotel to confirm that I met around middle up to end of March. I think it was the second week in March around --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's deal with Zdravkovski --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- probably --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- for a minute --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and let me finish, or we turn to a point where I answer your questions with "yes" or"no."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will you to answer the question, Mr. Hutsch, if you --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answer that we could take two other witnesses, and that this meeting with Mr. Zdravkovski took place in the in the Teteks textile file in Tetovo; and among these were Mr. Tastanovski, Minister Tastanovksi, and the manager from the Theke hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree, and I will put the question to you again, Mr. Hutsch, do you agree that, according to the statement of Mr. Zdravkovski, this meeting that you are alleging never took place? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that this statement is not contradicting your version?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you just meet somebody who is confirming that is what is written, I think we are wasting time. You don't need me for that, because you with present that to the Court or the Chamber without me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the question a third time, Mr. Hutsch. Do you agree that the statement made by Mr. Zdravkovksi in relation to the suggestion that you had a meeting with him at which he introduced to Mr. Tarculovski is contradicted by his statement? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we go to paragraph 7, Mr. Hutsch, it says this: "Secondly, I must say that, at the time of the events in Tetovo, I did not know who Johan Tarculovski was. I have never met Johan Tarculovski. I know him from the media." And at paragraph 8 it goes on to say: "On 18, 19 March 2001, I worked in the DBK state security and counter-intelligence. I was not the commander of the Tigri at the time." And at paragraph 9, he says: "I was not physically present in Tetovo at the time." And then at paragraph 10, it says: "The statement that I introduced Mr. Tarculovski to this journalist is false. As I have said, I did not know Mr. Tarculovski at the time, nor did the events that Mr. Hutsch talked about took place." And then at paragraph 12, he reiterates the fact that: "I became commander of the Tigri on 25th of May of 2001." So let me put these propositions to you, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's another witness who was taking part in this meeting that was a police officer, and I think it was a inspector, I'm not sure, who was works in the counter-drug section of the Ministry of Interior. He was trained in Germany in Buchholz in der Nordheide. Buchholz is written B-U-C-H-H-O-L-Z. This inspector also were in this -- in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me put the question to you, first, Mr. Hutsch. Would you agree that, according to the statement of Mr. Zdravkovski, the assertion contained in your statement contained at least five major contradictions with his statement, about the position which you claim Mr. Zdravkovksi had at the time, about his alleged presence in Tetovo at the time, about your alleged meetings and conversations with him, about the alleged meeting you, Mr. Zdravkovski, and Mr. Tarculovski, about Mr. Zdravkovksi acquaintance with Mr. Tarculovski, and there is actually a sixth about his role and position. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also refer for the transcript to the evidence of (redacted) of the 14th of June of 2007. I apologise. Could that be redacted, Your Honour, the name? I believe the name might have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be page 2108 and following about the date at which he ceased to be the commander of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, do you recall that you said you saw another individual in the village of Ljuboten on that occasion, a man called -- that you said was called Goran Stojkov. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that, again, there is no reference of Mr. Stojkov being present in Ljuboten in your notes of the 12th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that -- had you been informed -- or I should put it that way. Are aware of the fact that Mr. Stojkov was interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Stojkov told the Office of the Prosecutor that, on that date, he was in the town of Ohrid where the preparations for the Ohrid Agreement were being made?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that at that time Mr. Stojkov was the body-guard of the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated, I believe, in your statement, that when you first -- when you say you first met Mr. Stojkov in the village of Ljuboten, you say, you didn't know his last name. You knew him as Goran. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I believe, to the Prosecutor that you learned about his last name, you say, as Stojkov from another person. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you name the person who you say gave you the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my -- my language assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know where your language assistant got the name from?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go, Mr. Hutsch, for a moment to the 12th of August. That's Sunday. You've indicated in your evidence in chief and in your statement that you left the village at around 5.30, 1730. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall what road you took to go back from where you say you were on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were passing the road to Rastak and going over the -- the east road to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you go directly to Skopje at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had a meeting with some other people afterwards in the early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall who those people were?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters request the speaker not to overlap, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, we're being asked again to pause.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And, probably, may I have the transcript here on the screen. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Hutsch. I will ask the question again. Do you recall who those people were, the people that you had the meeting with, after you say you left the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you give the names of those people?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They don't have to do nothing with this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I will insist and ask you to give us the name, Mr. Hutsch, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is there any particular reason are you suggesting they are some of your sources again?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are interview partners of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you publish any paper in relation to these people?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you indicate what articles you published in relation to these people?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, things that were in context with the war in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more precise perhaps, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where did this meeting you, you say you had, take place?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the meetings was in the old Caravanserai, one of the restaurant in the old Muslim part of Skopje, and the other one took part in the area of the shoe factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, was anyone else present with you? Was anyone of your language assistant present with you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were in this moment the Albanian language assistant with me, but both meetings were done in German and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the interpreter is one of those persons you don't want to give the name of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall at what time those meetings, you say you had, finished?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1930, around.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And after that time, do you recall what you did?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the -- to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was your hotel in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Dal Met Fu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was that the hotel where you stayed?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that the same hotel that you stayed all that week?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated also that later, on that night, you went to the Dal Met Fu restaurant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is the restaurant which is part of the same hotel. Is that correct? And you indicated to the Office of the Prosecutor that around 8.00 p.m. on that night, the 12th of August, you saw Mr. Boskoski, you say, with a person you believe, or you say, was a person known by the nickname "Bucuk." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, again, that this is not something that you had put in your notes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the notes that -- that I that you have already, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Mr. Hutsch, that there are other notes which clue that pick meeting which you haven't given to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have notes for example with the number plate of a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will come to that particular issue in a moment. I wish to ask you a few questions about that. Did you know shows particular notes to the Prosecutor, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that you declined to provide the original of your notes to the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm talking about the 12th and the 14th, that you insisted to keep those and that you only gave a copy. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I gave the original notebooks from the 12th and 14th to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you kept the originals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. There's a document I'd like to show you, Mr. Hutsch. That's Rule 65 ter 1D304.1. Mr. Hutsch, what will appear in front of you is a statement of the director of the Dal Met Fu hotel, where you say you stayed that night on the 12th and also, as you just said, the rest of the week. It is a statement taken by the Defence ever Mr. Boskoski. I will read out what this person you said. His name is Branislav Dimitrov. At paragraph 1, he says: "I have been the director of the Dal Met Fu Bed and Breakfast Hotel in Skopje for many year, I think, since 1993 until present. The hotel has six rooms which is why it was registered as a bed and breakfast. I was the director in 2001, too. "Proper records are kept of all of the hotel guests in the register of guests. In keeping with the regulations, the register of guests must be kept for seven years. The register of guests for 2001 is kept in the hotel archives. All guests staying in our hotel are properly registered. When I was asked whether Franz-Josef Hutsch had been a guest in our hotel in 2001, I consulted the register of gusts before providing a answer." Paragraph 5 says: "Franz-Josef Hutsch was a guest in our hotel in August 2001. He stayed in room 14. The arrival was registered on 22nd August, 2001, and departure on 31st August, 2001. He proved his identity," -- sorry, "he proved his identify with an identity card issued by the Federal Republic of Germany, number 1078343868." So, in fact, Mr. Hutsch, isn't that correct that not only did you not stay at the Hotel Dal Met Fu, as you claim, during those days, but I am putting it to that you were not in Skopje at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's false. And I suggest to -- to have a look at the register, especially after the experience of the German government with the El Masri case, where hotel registries in Macedonia changed suddenly. There's another point wrong. An identity card has much more numbers than this one. So it is impossible, for example, and it is false, for example, that my identity was proved with a card number like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting to you, sir, that it's again one of those stories you have made and that, in fact, you did -- you were not where you claim to have been. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, if it is possible, I would like to answer in German.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe it should be so, if you would commence, we will check that it is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, can you start responding so we can verify whether the translation is working?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. [Interpretation] Mr. Mettraux, your hypothesis, that will not be any more true if you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case, Mr. Hutsch, I will show you a document which may assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Rule 65 ter 1D304.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that is coming up, Mr. Mettraux, would you please indicate the correct spelling of the name of the hotel and the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. It is, I believe, D-A-L, M-E-T, F-U, Dal Met Fu. Simply for Your Honours -- an indication to Your Honours, this is in e-court as one single document. This is the register of the hotel from page 1D00-2902 to page 1D00-2917. This is an English translation of the original which is to be found at pages 1D00-2886 to 1D00-2901 and it covers the period from 8, 9 August of 2001, to 30, 31st August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I wonder if only one of the document could be shown at this time so that the entire columns could be apparent on the screen.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I notice here is that in the original -- well, here you can see the English copy. But in the original, throughout the days, it's the same handwriting every day. But at that time there was not only a young woman, a young student working there, I think her name was Snjezana, but at the same there was a student of arts of who-- a male student of arts who was working in the reception, so I'm rather surprised that everything is written in the same handwriting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask you this, Mr. Hutsch: Do you know if, at the time when the six people that you see on the screen -- I'm sorry, they're actually five people. There was twice the same name. Do you know if, at the time when those people were registered or noted in the record, there were several people at entrance of the hotel at the reception? Are you aware -- are you-- Do you have knowledge after that fact?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few other guests there, I know that. I am not authorised to talk about one of the guests. The authorisation that I got from the German Minister of Defence, so I can't talk about that person. But the guests, I knew the guests, and one of them can confirm my presence there over a longer period of time. You could get this information through the German Ministry for Foreign Affairs and then the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask you my question once again, and I will ask to you answer it. Are you -- do you have knowledge that, at the time when the guests that appear on this particular page, that there had been several people in the reception of the hotel? Are you suggesting that you have knowledge of that fact?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of people present. It depended on when one was there. Usually, the young female student was there in the morning and the other male student was there in the afternoon and at noon time, and in the evening, I believe, but I'm not sure. I think there was -- the male student was there until about 10.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask you the question a third time, Mr. Hutsch. At the time when those particular guests were entered into the log-book, do you have knowledge of the fact that several people worked at the reception of the hotel, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one person there at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, if I can ask you the next question then, do you agree that your name doesn't appear on this particular page of the register. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the dates 10, 11 August, your name doesn't appear on the register of the hotel. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me the original in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be, I believe, starting at 1D00-2887.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, once again, that it is exactly the same handwriting for all the names written throughout, which is very, very much a surprise to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps can you answer my question. Do you see your name on this page, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page in the English, please, first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm quite satisfied with the Macedonian version here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll show you the English version first, Mr. Hutsch. Can you see your name anywhere on this page. That's the record of the 12 and 13 of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can Mr. Hutsch be shown the same page in Macedonian. That would be 1D00-2888, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's the same page in Macedonian, Mr. Hutsch. Do you see your name anywhere?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I do note here that from the number, 254, there is a different handwriting, which is very carefully written, very perfectly written.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... any suggestions to be made about that, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're the master of drawing conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm asking, Mr. Hutsch. That's the only --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only speculate here, and I don't wish to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree, a minute ago, you were saying that there was something suspicious about the fact that one person appeared to have written a number of record into the transcript. Do you recall that??

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on anything suspicious about the fact that a different person has written certain of the names there?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's rather strange, because all the guests would arrived at the same time, and there was only one -- if there was only one person there to write all the names down. I do know that the people, the guests arrived at different times of day. So there would be not this continuity and not such a system in the writing here. Here, from the 8th until the 13th of August, only one person was doing the work, and there is no deviation in the handwriting at all and I think that ought to be analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what about, perhaps, Mr. Hutsch, if there was one person that was making all those entries at once, do you think it is a possibility?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be odd, because I checked in with several different people and the other guests, too. They were met by different people. This is the experience that the German government had in the El Masri trial, too, the very same thing, which is also an investigative committee of the European commission, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's keep with that document for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry it to go to the next page in the English, please. That would be, I believe, 1D00-2905.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you see your name anywhere, Mr. Hutsch. It is the period 13, 14, 15 of --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you like to see the Macedonian as well?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could I please bring up 1D00-2889, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have any additional comments, Mr. Hutsch, to make on this page?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would only be repeating myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, can we turn to the next page, please, of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see your name anywhere on this page? This is the period 15 to 17 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see your name anywhere on the record. This is 16 to 18 of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, I was not in Skopje at that time;. I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see your name anywhere on this page, Mr. Hutsch, 17 to 19 of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the period covering 19 to 21st of August of 2001. Can you see your name anywhere?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the period from 20 August to 22 August. Can you see your name anywhere on this page?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I see the Macedonian original, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Of this particular page?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please bring up 1D00-2894.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know exactly what I'm going to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you wish to comment on this page, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see between the number 288, it should be 288 and 292, the numbers are wrong at the bottom. It should be a -- I think the 3 is wrong. And from the 21st of August, you can see number 288 and 299 or 293. It is the very same handwriting. There was absolutely no change of personnel in that hotel, so one person was present at the reception 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Or that was the person who would make the annotation in the book. Do you agree with that, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that is the reception book, you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. And you made a comment about the number, Mr. Hutsch, and I'm not sure that the transcript picked up exactly what you are suggesting. You said it should be 288 and 292. The numbers are wrong at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It started from 288, and I'm not sure whether that's 299 or 293. There are seven guests missing if the numbers are to continue in proper order.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In any case, the official translation of this Tribunal has interpreted that as being a "3," Mr. Hutsch, so that is 2-9-3, 293.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I would like it turn to the next page in the English, please. That is 1D00-2911.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can my colleague please clarify where the official interpreter of this Tribunal has clarified, not that it is the interpreter's business to clarify, but where the interpreter has clarified that the number is "293" as opposed to "299."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it is page 1D00-2910. This is the Defence document it is translated. It is a Defence document translated by CLSS. It is DEF 10057 Doc. I think the document is still on the screen, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I can see that now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, can you see your name on this page?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says it is number "296." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says,"Franz-Josef Hutsch, born 3rd April 1963, [indiscernible] Aachen, Germany," then it says, "ID card the Federal Republic of Germany," and then there's a number. It says that you stayed in room 14, and your arrival is noted as the 22nd of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what is not correct is the number of my identity card or my passport. It was not possible to enter Macedonia with -- with a identity card at the time. The number of the ID card, a German ID card, is much longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you recall from the top of your head what the identity card -- your identity card number is, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has -- it contains your birthday, and I don't see my birthday here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't it the record that German ID cards have on the top the general numbering. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Part of the number -- part of the number contains one's birthday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall arriving back from Germany on or around the 22nd of August of 2001, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's, again -- I'm sorry. You went to the Dal Met Fu hotel at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were registered as a guest in the log-book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show me the Macedonian of this page, too, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be 1D00-2896, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are under number 296, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is surprising here is that it looks like the handwriting of a older person; whereas, both of the people working at the reception were young people. The lady was in her early 20s. I think that was the first writing, handwriting we saw, but I'm not sure, and this handwriting here is certainly not the handwriting of a young student, a young person at the reception.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You are able, Mr. Hutsch, to approximate the age of a person by his or her writing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would seem to be indications here. I do not believe that this is the handwriting of a young person but this may be speculation on my part, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we turn please to the next page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Hutsch, that you were registered the next day as guest of the hotel. It is number 300. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 305, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 300, I believe and 305. You are correct twice, Mr. Hutsch, yes. One-- under 300, between the 23rd of August to the 24th of August; and under 305, between the 24th of August and the 25th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if we can turn to the next page. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You're recorded, under number 310, is that correct, between 25th of August to 26th of August, the same room?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You're recorded, again, under 314 for the period 26 to 27 of August.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Under 319 for 27, 28th August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, I'll ask you that. Do you recall how long you stayed? Did you stay in Macedonia after your return to Germany until that point in time when you started working for the embassy, or do you recall having had any trips abroad in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to verify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall going anywhere else in the country during this period, the end of the month, to, you say, the middle of September?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You mean in Macedonia, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check that. If I'm not mistaken, on the 31st, or is it the 30th? No, the 31st of August, or on the 1st of September it was, that I left Skopje and I think I went to Tetovo, because the German soldiers were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask you a question, Mr. Hutsch, first, about the record of the hotel. Do you agree that as far as this record of the hotel is concerned, and based also on the statement of the director of the hotel, these two documents suggest that, contrary to that you claimed, you did not stay in that hotel at any time during the time relevant to those events when you said that's where you stayed. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you have shown here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to go back to the events that you have mentioned on the 12th of August, you have indicated that you say you saw Mr. Boskoski with a man nickname "Bucuk" in the hotel -- I'm sorry, in the restaurant of the hotel Dal Met Fu at around 8.00. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct, Mr. Hutsch, that, at no time during the two interviews which you had with the Prosecutor, did you give any name or any nickname of this person which you have now identified as "Bucuk."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name "Bucuk," I learned the name in May or June of this year from a German official from the Landeskriminalamt in Hamburg, and I saw a photo of the fellow and noted that the photograph corresponded to the person that I had met. That was the occasion on -- when I first heard the name mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you mention the name of that German official, please, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know very well, and I think that was part of your evidence, the evidence that you have brought here, that contacts with the press -- there were contacts with the press, including with the speaker of Mr. Boskoski, and you know the context involved in such talks with journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you my question again, Mr. Hutsch. Could you please give the name of the German official who you say showed you a picture of the person you claim is "Bucuk"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would suggest that you contact the Landeskriminalamt in Hamburg.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the question a third time, Mr. Hutsch. Could you please give you a name of the German official which you claimed showed you a picture of the person whom you say is "Bucuk"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, the last four days we have been discussing German press law, and my answer is that in Germany we do have a law which protects one's sources, and I must protect my sources here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will ask that the person be asked to give the name of this particular official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have asked, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can I ask the Court to ask Mr. Hutsch to give the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'll do it for the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, are you able and willing to provide the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to use the Jonathan Wendell decision in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is your answer "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is your answer "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'm putting it to you that you are, once again, making up stories on the spot. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mettraux, Saint Augustine said, Hypotheses do not become more true when they with repeated, and he was a very wise man, Saint Augustine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that in December 2006, when the Prosecution interviewed you, you said didn't know the name of the man whom you claimed to have seen with Mr. Boskoski on the 12th of August, you say, in the Dal Met Fu restaurant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at the time, already, you were trying to associate Mr. Boskoski with this person "Bucuk." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the proofing stage, before the trial or before my evidence in July or June, we discussed this point and I mentioned the name "Bucuk." Mr. Saxon, who is very a very open and fair person, made a note about it which was disclosed to you. It is true that, while I was speaking to the Prosecutor, I did mention the name "Bucuk" but did not have a clear name or any particular details about this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you saying that in December of 2005 when -- of 2006, I apologise, or at any other time, you actually mentioned the name "Bucuk" in that context. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that I only learned the name much later, and it was during the proofing phase, in preparation for my testimony, that I did mention the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, during the preparation for your testimony, you conducted a investigation with the German police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was during research on another subject that it came up. I was shown a photo, and this name was mentioned in relation to organised crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are saying that the picture of Bucuk came by coincidence. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown the photo, and I do think I did recognise the person that I had seen earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But my question is were you researching this person in particular or are you saying that --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the picture came out by coincidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that, prior to that time, you had sought to link Mr. Boskoski to Mr. Bucuk in another way when you were being interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown a video-clip of a crowd of people with this individual in the crowd, and a Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also, Mr. Hutsch, that at the time you told the Prosecutor that you had taken down a number plate of a Mercedes who you say this person was driving at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he got into the Mercedes and then he drove off with it. Now whether he was the owner of this particular Mercedes, I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, but you gave a plate number, didn't you, to the Office of the Prosecutor about what you claimed were a car of Mr. Bucuk or a car in which he was driving. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You made a particular note of that fact, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you give those notes to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'm putting it to you that, again, this story is a fabrication by you and that Mr. Boskoski was not, in fact, at the restaurant Dal Met Fu on the 12th of August of 2001 around 8.00, as you testified. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I would only repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Will you please answer the question, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with you, also as I deferred in all other points with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D865.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is a statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of the former and then prime minister Mr. Ljupco Georgievski. Do you recall Mr. Georgievski as the prime minister at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask the registry to please turn to page -- page 4 of this document, please. That is 1D00- -- well, perhaps page 3 first. It is 1D00-7520. Can we go down to the last paragraph of that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, it is to show you the context of the questions that were being asked of the witness. He is being asked if Ljube Boskoski came to his office on Sunday, 12 August of 2001, and he says that he did not; and then the question that is relevant here is on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could please turn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if you can locate the first full sentence on that page, it starts with the word: "The next entry of my diary." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... "The next entry of my diary is that, at 7.00 p.m., I attended a co-ordinative meeting with a parliamentary group which was preparation for the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, which was due to happen the next day. The meeting, I believe, took place in Cair municipality building, but I'm not sure about this fact. I'm not sure, but I think that Ljube Boskoski also attended the meeting. "There were at least 50 people present there because our parliamentary group was quite large at that time. The whole parliamentary group was present at this meeting. Ljube Boskoski, as representative of the government, was supposed to be there; but, as I told, I am not sure about this. "I believe that I did not have any other conversation with Ljube Boskoski on Sunday of 12th of August, 2001, but, again, I'm not sure about this fact." So would it be a fair summary, Mr. Hutsch, to say that at -- starting at around 7.00 p.m., on the 12th of August, Mr. Georgievski attended what you said a co-ordinative meeting of his parliamentary group about the Ohrid Agreement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he believed, although he was not sure, that it took place in the Cair municipal building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you believed, but he wasn't sure, that Mr. Boskoski, as representative of the government, attended that meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness now please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1030.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What you will have on the screen, Mr. Hutsch, is a report by the police. It has been given to us by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we have the English version as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's entitled Report, Mr. Hutsch, and it says this: "During our working hours, between 8.00 and 20.00 hours, we acted according to order number 2396." It says: "A meeting took place at the VRMO-DPMNE, Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organisation Democratic Party for Macedonian National Unity, headquarters, where the following attended: Ljupco Georgievski, Ljube Boskoski, Nikola Gruev, as well as other deputies, accompanied with security personnel of 100 persons." Can you see that, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So do you agree that this document would, in fact, suggest that Mr. Boskoski attended the particular meeting. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, as a result, that he could not have been at two places at the same time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, if you haven't got any other proof, and if you read both texts, it doesn't tell you when Mr. Boskoski came to the meeting; and, secondly, I have got two different times, because it is given 19.00 hours, but here it says in the report that it was over at 8.00 p.m., 2000 hours. So I cannot understand your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the 19.00 hours, sir, was, according to Mr. Georgievski, the time at which the meeting started. The hours mentions here are the working hours of the gentleman -- or appears to be the working hours which the gentleman served in this capacity. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that, at the beginning of your testimony, I had asked you a number of questions about your sources of income in the year 2001. Do you remember me asking you that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was on the 28th of June, 2007, page 2843 to 2844, and you told me that your only source of income had been your work as a journalist. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I also asked you a question as to whether you had ever been a salesman and whether you had been in the business of selling clothes or coffins, and you said "no." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's at page 2843 to 2844. And, in your statement to the Prosecutor and, again, in your testimony here, you have indicated that, in your view as a journalist, it was very important to remain neutral and impartial. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... important not to be seen as siding with either of the two sides. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also said that you were merely a neutral observer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in the Milosevic trial, you also acknowledged having worked as a so-called embedded journalist with the KLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also explained to the Trial Chamber in the Milosevic case that, after your time in Kosovo, you kept in touch for several years with members of the KLA. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have also said that you had quite a number of contacts with the members of the NLA, this time in Macedonia, during your time in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you mentioned, I believe, that you met, in particular, with Mr. Gezim Ostreni known as "Plaku," about 75 to 85 time in a period of two month between, approximately, the middle of September to the middle of November. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that, in fact, you had at the time a business relationship at the time with Mr. Ostreni. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you, in fact, received money from Mr. Ostreni in the year of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you received money from Mr. Ostreni because you were selling goods to him. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber why you received money from Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, this is not covered. I have started saying by I have the son [as interpreted], but this is not covered my agreement of my ability of giving evidence. I have to ask you to look into that, whether I can actually say something, because otherwise this would be a punishable offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The first document which the Defence would seek to tender at this stage, although I should mention for the record also, that it has been put quite extensively to Mr. Hutsch in his evidence, but we believe it may be important for the Chamber to have the full article. It is the article from the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung of the 3rd of May of 2001 prepared by Mr. Rub, journalist for the FAZ, and it talks, inter alia, about reports and the testimony of Mr. Hutsch. This is it Rule 65 ter 1D280. This is tab 11 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I was simply going to ask what tab of the binder it was, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Tab 11, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D254. This would be tab 51 of the binder. This is, again, an article prepared by Mr. Hutsch, this one on the 15th of August of 2001. It is called, "Macedonia: Who is warning to watch out for Albanian Tricks." It was shown to Mr. Hutsch, in particular in relation to the matter of Tetovo and the location of Mr. Hutsch at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D255. This is, again, a piece written by Mr. Hutsch. This one on 16 August 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the counsel please slow down when they mention difficult facts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The title of the document is,"Macedonia: Count down for the German Army Deployment," and it is again a piece written by Mr. Hutsch. It was, again, put to Mr. Hutsch in the context of his cross-examination for the same purpose as the previously document. It is tab 52, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D243.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is to be found under tab 76 of the binder. It is Rule 65 ter 1D304.2, and it is the record of the Dal Met Fu hotel in Skopje, both in English and in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would object to the admission of this document at this time. Not only could this witness not speak to how this document was created or prepared, the witness suggested that entries in the document were either incorrect or falsified. So, in the submission of the Prosecution, it would not be appropriate to tender this document via this witness. If the Defence likes, they can certainly bring the person or persons who purportedly created this document during their Defence case and discuss it then, but we don't believe this is it the appropriate time or manner to receive this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps a brief reply. Two matters: I believe the issue of reliability or otherwise of a document will be for the Chamber assess and not for the witness. The second matter which Mr. Saxon has raised is the issue of the person who took those notes, and, indeed, we have presented a short statement from the director of the hotel to Mr. Hutsch. It will be the Defence decision to decide whether or not the witness should be called whether live or as a Rule 92 bis witness, which in turn may have, and perhaps it would have, some relevance to the issue of weight, if any, to give to this document. However I don't understand the Prosecution to be suggesting that the documents is false or otherwise. This document was obtained by the Defence from the hotel directly, and I don't understand Mr. Saxon to make a issue of authenticity. If, as Mr. Saxon believes, they are some issues in relation to the reliability of this document, we believe it can be a issue of weight, and the document should therefore be admitted, we believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber would take the view it should be marked for identification, Mr. Mettraux, and not admitted as a document, because the witness does not accept it as accurate and cannot otherwise speak about its content.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour. In that case, I will move on to the next -- I move on to the next document on the list. Yes, I'm sorry. The marking has to be made.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D244, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, which we would seek to tender at this stage, is under tab 107 of the binder. This is Rule 1D370, and this was the record made about the dispute between Mr. Hutsch and the FAZ. It is published in the FAZ, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, and it is dated the 11th of June of 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D245, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, which we'd seek to tender at this stage, was actually on it's Prosecution Rule 65 ter list. This is Rule 65 ter 216.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm informed it now has a 1D number as well. It is also 1D925, Your Honour. This is a daily log sheet dated the 12th of August of 2001. It comes from the archives of the OSCE, and it was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor. Your Honour will recall that it contains a number of references to a crowd of people in or around the village of Radisani on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D246.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, there are simply two other documents which we would at this stage as the Chamber marked for identification, and those would the two transcript of the telephone conversations which were played to Mr. Hutsch. They would be 1D319, that's Rule 65 ter 1D319; and Rule 65 ter 1D318. We understand there is a CD with the documents on it, if it -- it has to be marked separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not object to having these transcripts marked for identification at this time; however, I'm wondering whether my colleague could tell us anything about where these recordings were made, who recorded them, where they come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage, the Defence will ask not to disclose the identity of the person who provided us with those documents. This is the reason why we do not seek to tender these documents: We have been asked by the person, in the form of Rule 70, not to disclose the origin of this particular document, so we used simply to elicit evidence from Mr. Hutsch at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I address the Chamber on this briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon? It simply seems to me, Your Honour, that now the Prosecution is at a disadvantage, because whether or not the transcripts or the recordings of these intercepts are eventually admitted into evidence in the future of this case, it is my understanding that they have become part of the record of these proceedings. I think in fairness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They do not stand as evidence. They're marked for identification, held in the court record, so that if in future reference is made to the document that was put to the witness, the document is identified and can you produced. But they are not evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would that be true, Your Honour, in addition to the interpretation of the recordings that were -- become part of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, that's happened in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we're like two ships passing in the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. I'm making it very clear to you what marking the document does. It doesn't make it a exhibit. There has been something played to the witness in court. We know nothing about that, its source or its authenticity, except that which that which Mr. Hutsch has in some way, expressly or impliedly, perhaps acknowledged.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Tab 84 will be marked for identification, which I think is the first of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. 319, Your Honour, 1D319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit 1D247, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then tab 86 will be -- 85, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D248, Your Honours, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour, I believe that is all at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I continue, Mr. Mettraux, turning from Mr. Mr. Saxon to you about those two document that have just been marked. Your failure to indicate in any way their source, at the moment, could well lead to some significant delay at a later stage in the trial, because if you seek, in some way, to establish these documents, it is quite probably that the Prosecution would want time to investigate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We understand that, Your Honour. And we -- we will discuss the matter further with the Prosecution with a view, perhaps, to see whether there is a means to work things with Mr. Saxon that would not put him at a disadvantage, should he think that is indeed a matter that needs to be investigated, and we will also contact the source in question that provided us with this material. We are grateful for your indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, may I? [Interpretation] I would like to say something here. As we're talking about evidence, I'd like to add something, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hutsch. We're almost abandoning some of our normal rules, so we might as well continue it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence mentioned an article that I had brought, which were said to be originals the day before yesterday. When I went out of the room, I happened to see on the table there a -- the report, and I noticed there were some substantial differences from the original. The original is here in my hand, and the other one is different. I saw on the screen that Mr. Mettraux had been using the online versions of the Hamburger Adenblatt. And, of course, one would have to see when these reports were put on line, because this involves the conclusions that Mr. Mettraux made. So I have all the articles here in the originals, and you will be able to see the difference. And, I think, Mr. Mettraux, you will be able to realise that I have worked on your behalf to get all these articles ready for you, so that you can see the originals and can you compare them to the original versions in the Hamburger Adenblatt and not use the on line versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply for the record, perhaps the version that we handed to the Chamber yesterday, whether the original in the sense of the, I think, PDF copy that was provided to us from the Hamburger Adenblatt, Mr.. Hutsch is correct that the version that was shown to him was from the Internet; however, Your Honour in their possession have the original, which we received from the newspaper in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Mettraux. That may help, Mr. Hutsch, a little. I would further observe, just to bring this back on to the normal procedural lines, train lines, that is, that if Mr. Saxon seeks to put in the original of the articles, they would be received by the Chamber. If in the time which he will have between now and when he completes his re-examination, he is able to see whether there are material difference from what we have, which may, I suspect, be exactly what you have there. Thank you for bringing it to our attention. Now, Mr. Apostolski, are there questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I do have questions for this witness; however, I will need some time to prepare with consultation with Mr. Mettraux. Is it perhaps a good time for a break or that I consult with him privately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will, I think, we can accommodate you, Mr. Apostolski. If we have the second break now, resuming at 25 minutes to 1.00, that will give you an hour and ten minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
