utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now the hour and ten minutes, we still have this hope that we will be able to finish, Mr. Hutsch, today, bear in mind. But I see, I expect that, even now, it may be beyond us now to finish, Mr. Hutsch, by 1.45 today. But both you and Mr. Saxon, I'm sure will be mindful of the time; and if it is possible, we'll finish. But the cross-examination, so far, has gone on to a considerable time and has involved many issues, and it may that be it is quite impossible for Mr. Saxon to deal with what we wishes to deal with in the time that now remains. But, certainly, we are in a position now to feel that we can conclude Mr. Hutsch's evidence by tomorrow when he needs to be away. We resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for taking more time, but I have been asked to specify for the record the fact that MFI 1D247 and MFI 1D248, which were the last two documents which were MFI'd, contained both the transport and the audio which was played. The second matter which we would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber is a document, which is Exhibit 1D224. It is a document from the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany which was shown to Mr. Hutsch, and also I believe to at least one or two witnesses. We have now received the official translation from CLSS of that document, and the registry will take care of placing the right document on the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness Hutsch. My name is Antonio Apostolski; and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic, we're the Defence counsel of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Witness, I have several questions to put to you today in connection with the events in Ljuboten in the year 2001. Are you ready to begin?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that, when you entered the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001, you recognised two persons: Johan Tarculovski and Goran Stojkov. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Prosecution took two statements from you on the 25th, 26th, and 27th of October, 2005, and the second statement on 3rd and 4th July and 9th of December, 2006?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that, in giving the first statement, you were shown a video-clip on which you recognised persons -- or rather, you recognised Mr. Goran Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. I don't know if it was one complete videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. And, on this clip, you recognised Mr. Goran Stojkov. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that, while giving the interviews to the Prosecution, you did not carry out recognition of Mr. Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not identify Mr. Johan Tarculovski while giving the statement to the Prosecution with the pictures or the video-clips?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you will concur with me that, with the help of photographs and video-clips, you did not identify Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You previously stated that you were acquainted with Mr. Goran -- with Mr. Jaculovksi [as interpreted] -- with Goran -- by Mr. Goran Zdravkovski during the fighting at the Cali in Tetovo. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were introduced by Mr. Goran at the front line?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On this occasion, you spoke with Mr. Tarculovski about the current situation at the front line. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a short talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this conversation was carried out directly with Mr. Tarculovski without the help of an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you spoke with Mr. Johan through an interpreter in the Macedonian language. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that Goran, who introduced us went and translated the sentences briefly, and I read this recently in one of the articles, the road in question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like to hear your answer. Can you tell me, please, whether you spoke with Mr. Johan through a interpreter, or, as you would like to say now, that interpretation was done by Mr. Goran Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the latter.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it is correct that Mr. Goran Zdravkovski translated interpreted for you. Let us clear this up. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, if I were to put it to you that Mr. Johan Tarculovski knows English fluently, would you agree with me that you had no need to use Mr. Goran Zdravkovski as an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. We -- I spoke German and English with Goran; and, in general terms, we talked about the situation at that locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. It is not of interest what you spoke about, rather, the language in which you spoke; therefore, you want to say that Goran Zdravkovski speaks English and German. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few words of German, and he spoke English.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the first page of the statement of Mr. Goran Zdravkovski of the 24th of October, 2005, given to the Prosecution, 2D00-175.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on the screen the statement of Mr. Goran Zdravkovski in the Macedonian and English language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this is his information; and in line 7, I believe this is where it's -- where it is written "spoken languages," but the only language which is listed is the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you then agree with me that Mr. Goran Zdravkovski did not mention that he knows you the English or German languages? Can you give a "yes" or "no" answer. You don't have to give a explanation.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Mr. Johan Tarculovski lived in Austria for a period of three years with his former wife, and that he knows the German language as well, he knows and uses the German language, would you agree with me that would you have no need to use Goran Zdravkovski as a interpreter, since we have a situation which is quite the contrary to what you say, that Goran Zdravkovski does not know these languages, while Johan Tarculovski does?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to say? What do you want me to answer with a "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that did you not have the need and you did you not use, as you have stated in front of this Court, Mr. Goran Zdravkovski as a interpreter?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that did you not meet with Mr. Johan Tarculovski in Tetovo in March 2001 at all, as was also stated by Mr. Goran Zdravkovski in his statement which my colleague Mr. Mettraux pointed out to you. Is this correct? This was also said in his statements to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I put it to you that you did not meet with Johan Tarculovski in the March of 2001. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Just a while back, you said that you met with him in a cafe in Tetovo, and that Mr. Tastanovski can confirm this, as well as the director of the factory Teteks. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you were speaking about the textile factory from Tetovo, that you know its director, is it correct that you were talking about the factory for textiles called "Teteks"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the director of this factory is?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I must restrict my answers, too. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that his name is Niko -- is it correct that his name is "Gligorie Gogovsky"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you do not know that Mr. Gligorie Gogovsky is the director of the Teteks factory?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I could describe the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me what his height is?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: One metre 80, to one metre 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me his age?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would be in his mid 40s, early 50s.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: A sort of grey mixture.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Black and grey?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, if I were to tell you that this person is 65 years of age and was a former prime minister of the Republic of Macedonia in the 1990s and that his height is one metre 72 centimetres, would you concur with me that you gave me wrong information about this person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For you claim that your information is correct, the information which you have just provided?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the name, and here you're describing a person, this person, the person I met.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm giving a precise description of the person who is the director of Teteks.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purpose of the record, he said that you have met with him on page 3 of today's transcript, line 12. This is for the purpose of the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will continue with a different topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt. Just one point of clarification. The director that my colleague Mr. Apostolski is referring to, he has been using the present tense, "is," "is the director." I'm sorry. That is how it was interpreted to me. He is referring to the person who was the director in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For clarification to my learned colleague, my questions pertain to March 2001, and please be informed that the director of this factory, starting from 1992 up until today, is the director of this factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that you saw Johan sitting in a white Cherokee Jeep in Ljuboten on the 12th of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that this Jeep was coming from the western part of Ljuboten when you met?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The Jeep was coming towards you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your interpreter waved and the Jeep stopped, is this correct, waved with his hand.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Johan was sitting in the co-pilot seat?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The window of the Jeep was open, and your interpreter spoke in the Macedonian language with Johan. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were sitting [as interpreted] one metre from the door. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The transcript should read "standing."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you standing one metre from the door?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you seeing -- I will reformulate the question. Did you stand one metre from Johan's side or the driver's side?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the co-pilot's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the -- Jeeps are taller than passenger vehicles, especially this model of Jeep, Cherokee?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. I don't know. I didn't measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was -- is Cherokee Jeep higher than a normal passenger vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it a terrain vehicle, a four-wheel vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And your interpreter spoke with Mr. Johan through the open window. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me, is it correct that, when the Jeep stopped, Johan opened the window, or was the window previously opened? Can you tell me this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] The window was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this mean that you could only see the head and the upper part of the body of Mr. Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You could see the upper part of his uniform?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this was black in colour?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you saw that, on the bottom, he wore black trousers. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And, if any person claims before this Court that, on the day of 12th of August, 2001, Johan was dressed in camouflaged uniform, then this witness would be giving false testimony.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it as being black.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that if anyone were to say before this Court that Johan was wearing a camouflage uniform, that this would not be the truth?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm here to tell what you I saw, not to draw conclusions from what you think I might have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also stated before this Court, when you saw Johan in Ljuboten in the Jeep, he was wearing a pistol, a revolver on his right leg. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, can you tell me where Johan was wearing this gun?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to consult with my interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see, and did you testify before this Court, that he was wearing a gun? You told us the brand, Glock, an Austrian handgun.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is on page 2776.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And can you now tell us whether Johan was wearing this gun?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was told, I think it was on his upper hip, on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On his right hip, is this correct, or on the upper part of his leg, on his thigh?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upper thigh.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: Did the gun have a holster.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to ask my interpreter at the time, but the weapon must have been attached to his hip somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you claim that your interpreter told you this, but you did not see this. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown his statement, 65 ter 2D00-76.126; page 17 in the English version and 19 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this on the screen? Do you see your statement on the screen? Can you read that it says here -- do you see it first? My question: Do you see the statement on the screen? It is said -- this is what you said to the Office of the Prosecutor when you gave your statement, and it was also said in the transcript, page 2776, when you testified before this Court: "I was immediately after -- behind the place where he was sitting. I was looking at the vehicle. I saw that Johan Tarculovski was wearing a holster on the right side. It was a pistol holster for the upper part of his right leg. It was equipped with a 9-millimetre pistol Glock automatic pistol. This was clear to me. And based on my military and professional experience, I'm 100 percent sure that this was this type of weapon." Witness, can you confer with me that just a while back, before this Court, you stated that did you not see this, that it was your interpreter that saw this. And before this Court, you have stated the same as before the Office of the Prosecutor, when giving your statement, something all together contrary to this, that you even recognised the brand of the pistol. Can you agree with me that these two -- that this is contradictory?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not contradictory for the following reason: Because in all this material, what the team saw -- well, for instance, I said that I telephoned, and then it was found out later that that was not accurate, that I had personally been telephoning, but we as a team had telephoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, by my colleague, Mettraux, that is to say, to your statement of the 27th of June, 2007: [In English] "I think he was warning a leg holster with a Glock pistol." [Interpretation] This is what you stated before this Court on the 27th of June, 2007.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you show me where the contradiction lies?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The contradiction is in the fact that, to this Court, you have stated that your interpreter had seen this and told this about this, while you here say that you have seen it. Is it correct that everything which you have seen or what you're telling this Court is, in fact -- are, in fact, things which you have not seen, and that these are events which were retold to you by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In line 8, what I see what you are reading as an apparent quotation, in line 8, it is not true that I said I had seen that it was a Glock pistol. On the contrary, it says, "I think." But you can correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you read paragraph 126 out loud, please - this is the statement which is in front of you - so that there is no confusion?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "I was directly standing beside him, not more than half a metre. I was standing slightly behind his seating position. I was looking inside the car. I have seen that Johan Tarculovski was wearing a holster on his right side. It was a pistol holster for the upper part of his right leg. It was equipped with a 9-milimetre Glock automatic pistol. This was clear to see. And based on my military and professional experience, I'm 100 percent sure that it was this type of this weapon."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this would mean you're 100 percent sure that what you have seen, it was really a Glock pistol?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, I am certain, that is, with a photograph, we were able to identify what a kind of pistol it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I don't need a photograph to identify. You were the one who identified in your statement. I don't have a clue about weapons. You know about this stuff. You're a military expert, so that I don't need it. I would like to ask you further --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't saying that were supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you told this Court that you know Mr. Tarculovski, and that you know that he was born in Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You claim that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was born in Ljubanci. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the house of his father, the father of Johan Tarculovski, is at the entrance of the village of Ljubanci, on the right-hand side when you go into the village from Radisani. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And this was something that was told to you, or this is something you know and you claim before this Court? How sure is this information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a piece of information that I did not check.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you confirm this statement and whether it is correct or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any confirmation that this house was there -- I was actually there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this is an untruthful information, the information you provided in your statement to the investigators from the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please show me, again, the statement pertaining to this particular item?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I will show it to you now. I just wanted to ask you whether you told the investigators that you are not quite sure about this.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could you show me what I've asked for?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to answer the question, first of all, whether you told the investigators from the ICTY about the fact that you knew where the -- Johan Tarculovski's father house is, and, actually, that you are not quite sure about it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I used the German conjunctive form, the subjunctive.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown, please, 65 ter 2D00-076, page 25. Page 25 in the Macedonian version; in the English version, page 23, paragraph 162.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the document, the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please read out loud paragraph 162, please. This is your statement that you provided to the ICTY investigators.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] "I know Johan Tarculovski since the year of 2001. The first time I met Johan Tarculovski at around 18, 19 March 2001 in Tetovo. It was the time before the offensive on the Mount Kale. I know that he was born in Ljubanci and that his father's house is in the entrance of the village, right side, coming from Radisani."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you gave wrong information to the investigators in this particular paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should have made the statement in German. Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A little while ago, you said that you gave the statement in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please close the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that a while ago you said that you provided the statement in German language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your statement that you provided to Mr. Thomas Kuehnel, on the 25th, 26th, and the 27th of August, was given in German language.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about -- we talked in German. Mr. Kuehnel then translated it into English; and then, again, it was marked by a native speaker, corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the first page of his statement, 65 ter 2D00-676. This is the Macedonian version. Could we see the English version, please, as well. Can we see the bottom lines in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see, at the very bottom of the page, your signature on this statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see in front of you which were the languages used during the interview?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see what does say here? It says "English."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this is completely different and opposite to what you told me earlier, that German was the language used?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we can get hold of Mr. Kuehnel, and he is going to confirm my statement that we were speaking in German, then he translated the statement into English, and then, again, this statement was translated into English again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see in front of you the wording where it says "interpreter"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see it says "no interpreter," or "none."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that there was no interpreter during the time when you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So you would agree with me that the statement you gave, regarding the fact that you knew where Johan Tarculovski's father house is, is a incorrect statement, a statement that you provided to the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the information you gave is correct about the location of Mr. Johan's father's house in the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown again his statement, page 23 in the English version and page 25 in the Macedonian version, paragraph 162, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you're trying to say that what you stated in paragraph 162 is true.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I hadn't checked this, and I didn't research. Again, I didn't do my own research where the house was located and where --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter didn't acoustically hear what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that all the other information provided to the Prosecution office, and information you gave before the Court, have not been checked, like it is the case with this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already explained yesterday that the telephone conversations that I had, and the statements of the people I talked to, that I did not verify them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm just ask being this information and all the rest of the information, so we are talking about unconfirmed information. Does it mean that all other information that you provided before this Court have not been properly checked, and this is information you received over the phone?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, because some information has been verified; and, in some parts, it is hasn't been verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So this means some of them have been verified, some of them not, the information you provided before this Court. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you did not tell the investigators and this Court which of this information has been verified and which have not been verified?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. This is very honest on your part. In the village of Ljuboten, on the 12th of August, you saw and recognised a person Goran Stojkov. This is something you mentioned earlier and you confirmed. You also confirmed that he was wearing a black overall, the same type like Johan, and he also spoke with your interpreter in Macedonian language. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you further claim that, on the 12th of August, you spoke to Mr. Goran Stojkov through your interpreter in the village of Ljuboten. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a person called Goran and where I did not have any surname at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you testifying here today that you saw a person named Goran and that you are not sure; this is to say, it is not true that this was the person called Goran Stojkov?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please answer me: Is it true that you saw the person Goran Stojkov in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001, and can you be 100 percent sure about it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to show me a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is something you stated before this Honourable Court, and this is something you stated before the investigators of the ICTY in your statement. So this is something you said on the 27th of June, on page 2781, line 17.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, show me the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you whether this is an information that you corroborated, verified?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person that I saw there was identical to a person who later on was also known in the public under the name of Goran Stojkov.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So now you claim that Goran Stojkov was in the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001. Is this what you testify? Like I already mentioned, this is something you said on the 27th of June, and also in your statement. A bit later, I will show your statement provided to the ICTY investigators.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember very well this statement; and, in this statement, I also said that we met a person who was called Goran and about whom later on I learned that he was called Goran Stojkov. Also, this person --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown paragraph 132, page 20 in the Macedonian version, and page 18 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see you in front of you, the statement?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have stated here that Goran Stojkov was dressed in the same manner like Johan Tarculovski, and he had a black overall with a regular police insignia and he didn't wear a helmet: "I could only see that he a handgun in a holster. He did not have a Kalashnikov. It was interesting to see that just Stojkov wore a black uniform, and the other subordinate policemen were wearing a regular camouflage uniform." Is this something that you have stated and you have said before the ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that, in this statement, you claim that only Stojkov was wearing a black uniform, and this is different to your previous statement when you said that Mr. Tarculovski was also wearing a black uniform?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're taking the statement apart, because it says in paragraph 131, it says -- it says that it was about asking whether, in the group that he was part of, whether there were other people wearing a black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. But would you agree with me that you saw Goran Stojkov then and is this what you testify here today, or this is also an information that you haven't verified and you're not quite sure about it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person, or the persons that I saw, I saw again under the name of Goran Stojkov, who was then promoted to a police general, to be a police general.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your testimony, before this Honourable Court, is that you have seen Goran Stojkov? Please answer with "yes" or "no," the same way when you are replying to the Prosecutor, in the same way as it is in your statement.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is in 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will ask you kindly to respond to my question, to give me a very simple "yes" or "no" answer. Did you see the person Goran Stojkov on the 12th of August, 2001 in the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot reply to that question by "yes" or "no," as it's implied in the first two sentence under 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So what can be seen in paragraph 132 in your statement is incorrect, and I kindly ask you to answer whether you have seen the person Goran Stojkov in the village of Ljuboten. On page 2782, you confirmed that you have seen him, then I won't be bothering you any further with these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the statement provided by Nikovski Toni.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please answer this question: Whether the information was verified, whether it was 100 percent correct and verified that you saw Goran Stojkov in the village of Ljuboten. Please answer this question with "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That was a fairly long question by my learned colleague. It started out with this: "So what can be seen in paragraph 132 in your statement is incorrect," then it went further and he asked Mr. Hutsch to answer whether he had seen Mr. Stojkov, and then Mr. Apostolski seems to be moving on to show a statement. I think, to be fair to the witness, he should have a right to respond to what Mr. Apostolski is arguing, for lack of a better word, that is what is said in paragraph 132 of his statement is incorrect, rather than stating his argument in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked this witness on a number of occasions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please respond with a "yes" or a "no" whether your information about the location of Goran Stojkov in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001 is 100 percent correct? Please respond with a "yes" or a "no."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, there is information that was not verified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is your conclusion, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's a mistake in translation. It should read the question: "Whether your information about the fact that you saw Mr. Goran Stojkov was verified, was checked."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this information checked?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You visited Ljuboten and the place where Rami Jusufi was killed on the 14th of August, 2001. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You visited his house. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, on the 14th of August, 2001, you were in the village but did not visit the house of Rami Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only in the garden, in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it is correct that you visit the courtyard, his courtyard, on the 14th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The body of Rami Jusufi was taken away and you did not see it. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You noticed, you marked this down, and you noted this in your notes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You saw that the door from the courtyard was down, was torn down?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "torn down"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The gate of the front yard was broken, blown up.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have the impression that the gate was blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was the gate in a normal position? The front -- the gate to the yard, was it in a normal state?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right door of the gate was open, and the left door was open to, say, 30 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see the vehicle set on fire by the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you answered inside, in the courtyard, and you did not see any kind of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the courtyard, you saw a passenger vehicle which was allegedly set on fire by the Macedonian security forces. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, this vehicle was in a normal state.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us the state of this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was burnt out.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this a passenger vehicle, Zastava?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: These are vehicles which were produced in Yugoslavia. Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where Zastava was manufactured?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know the state in which Volkswagen is produced?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in over 45 different countries on this planet.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you could agree with me that Zastava is not manufactured in Volkswagen?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which licences have been given for the manufacturing of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know the vehicles Golf, of the brand Golf?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: There is a Golf Model I?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Golf II, III, IV and V, do you know this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know all types of Golf? Would you be able to recognise Golf I as a mark?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What about Golf II?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Golf III?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Golf IV?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Golf V?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Previously, you said that you recognised the brand is Golf. Which of these Golfs are you able to recognise?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment, all I can say is that it was a Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 1D2, 1D22 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1D2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the vehicle which you saw?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the door which you saw?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you claim that this is a vehicle of the Zastava brand. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is time to adjourn today, and I would like to make mention to the Court about the presence of Goran Stojkov in Ljuboten. The statement, 6281 and 6282 of the 16th of October, 2007 is the statement given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn then for the day, to resume at 9.00 in the morning to conclude this witness and then to move on to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
